about: Who each of a person's own records is shared with, as DATA the one sharing owner reads (src/record-sharing.mjs). Which fields a share copies is src/space-settings.json share_from_private, never a list here; this file only names how those fields read on the sharing sheet (`fields`: per kind, per field, its `label`, and `show`, the path read inside the value when the value is an object, or `each`, the path read inside every item when the value is a list, one line per item; `words`, plain words for a value or for the start of one, the longest start that fits; `as`, how a value reads: `date` its day, `size` a count of bytes) and which records link to which (`links`), so a record can be shared together with the records it links to. A link { from, field, to } says a record of kind `from` names records of kind `to` in `field` (an id, a list of ids, or an object keyed by ids). `chain` is the switch's words per kind. `kinds` is how each kind of record is named to a person (the Shared with me screen). `places` are the words and icons of the three kinds of place a record can go: the network (anonymous learning and stories), a space, a person. The network's `follows_account` names the kinds of record the account's own network choice decides when a record has no choice of its own; every other kind with no choice of its own stays with the person alone. `refused` are the words said when a read or a share is refused by the owner's choice. Every link opens on /share/<code>, whatever it shares. `delivery` is the email a link made for one email address sends to that address when the person sends it (POST /sharing/<record>/links/<share_id>/send): per kind, or `default`, its subject, preheader, words and button, filled with {sender} (the sharer's name, or `someone` when the account has none fit to show) and {title} (the record's title); `note_heading` introduces the sharer's own words when they add some; `kind` names these emails for the one sender's per-person limits (src/mail-settings.json). `abilities` are what a link lets its recipient do beyond seeing it (each { id, label, icon, needs_proof }): `offered` names, per kind of record (or `default`), the abilities a link to that kind may carry, and `given` the ones a new link carries when the sharer names none; an ability a page has no way to perform is never offered. `needs_proof` means the recipient proves an email address (a one-time code, no account needed) before acting, so a payment or a signature always names someone. `when_facts` are the facts a link's own condition (`when`, a rule tree in the formula engine's shape) may name: each reads the clock (`from: clock`), the link itself (`from: grant`, a path in it) or the shared record (`from: record`, a path in its value), with `unset` the value a fact has before anything set it, so a link that opens only after a date, closes after it was signed, or opens once a record reaches a state is one rule, never code. `proof` is every word the page says while a recipient proves their email. `parts` are the pieces of a record that can be shared on their own: a part is `<whole>:<id>:<segment>:<part id>`, shared as its whole narrowed to that one piece (one row of a list), by link or email only. `look` is how the recipient page carries a brand: the sharer's own (name, logo, colour, kept once per account) or Trillion's, and `made_with` is the line every recipient page ends with whichever brand it carries. file_dependencies declares exact workspace relation paths for related immutable file parts. These links are read through the current addressed workspace owner and checked under the original file grant; filenames never establish a relationship.

sealed.label: Only my devices can open this
sealed.detail: Sealed on this device with your passphrase. Trillion keeps it but cannot read it, and your AIs cannot either.

page_words.heading: A sealed record shared with you
page_words.reading: Opening it with the key in this link.
page_words.role_writer: You can read it. Changing it is done from Trillion on a device that holds the key.
page_words.no_key: This link has lost its key. A sealed link only opens as it was copied, with everything after the # sign. Ask for the whole link again.
page_words.wrong_key: This link's key does not open this record. It may have been copied in part, or the record was sealed again.
page_words.unavailable: This sealed record could not be fetched. The link may have been stopped.

link_words.heading: Share it with a link only the key opens
link_words.lead: The link carries its own key after the # sign. Trillion keeps only the sealed copy and never sees the key, so anyone with the whole link can read it and nobody else can.
link_words.made: Link ready. Copy it now: Trillion cannot show it again.
link_words.failed: The link could not be made. Try again.
link_words.needs_copy: Making this link needs a copy kept on this device, opened with your passphrase.

sealed.shared_first: Stop sharing it first: once sealed, it is shared only by a sealed link that carries its own key.
sealed.about_links: A sealed link shares a sealed record without Trillion reading it: the person's device seals a copy with a fresh key of the link's own (parts/sealed-records sealForLink) and sends only that sealed copy, { content_id, value }; the key rides in the link's fragment, which no browser sends to a server. link_roles are what a link's holder may do, each { id, label, can, granted_by_link }: can is the link's abilities (abilities.list); a role with granted_by_link false is never given by a link. A writer replaces the sealed copy only by naming the content_id it replaced (compare-and-set). Stopping the link drops its sealed copy.
sealed.role_refused: A sealed link gives one of these roles: {roles}.
sealed.only_sealed_link: A sealed record is shared only by a sealed link: send the copy your device sealed for it (sealed_copy).
sealed.not_sealed_record: Only a sealed record is shared by a sealed link.
sealed.not_listed: A sealed link is never listed: only someone holding the link can open it.
sealed.not_sealed_link: This link does not carry a sealed copy.
sealed.changed: Someone changed this sealed copy first. Open the link again, then make your change.

refused.not_shared_with_you: This is not shared with you.
refused.not_shared_here: You chose not to share this here. Change who it is shared with first.
refused.unknown_place: That is not one of your pursuits, or someone you share a pursuit with.

default.subject: {sender} shared {title} with you
default.preheader: Open it with a one-time code sent to this email address.
default.markdown:
{sender} shared **{title}** with you on Trillion.

Open the link and confirm this email address with a one-time code. No Trillion account needed.

tool.subject: {sender} shared a tool with you: {title}
tool.preheader: Your AI can run it from your own Trillion while the link is open.
tool.markdown:
{sender} shared **{title}** with you on Trillion.

Open the link to see what it does. To use it, give the link to your AI in Trillion: it runs the tool in your own account, with your own connections, for as long as {sender} keeps the link open.

sales-contract.subject: {sender} sent you a deal: {title}
sales-contract.preheader: Review and sign the terms with a one-time email code.
sales-contract.markdown:
{sender} put together **{title}** for you.

Open the link and confirm this email address with a one-time code to review and sign. No Trillion account needed. If the deal has a price, you can pay after signing.

proof.heading: Open what {sender} shared
proof.body: Enter your email. We will send you a 6-digit code. No account needed.
proof.body_named: This was shared with one email address. Enter it and we will send you a 6-digit code. No account needed.
proof.code_body: If this was shared with {email}, a 6-digit code is on its way. It works for 10 minutes.
proof.wrong_code: That code is not right, or it has ended. Send a new one.
proof.too_many: Too many codes were asked for. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
proof.sign_in_instead: Have a Trillion account? Sign in
proof.phone_needs_sign_in: This was shared with one phone number. Sign in to Trillion with that number to open it.

email.subject: Your code: {code}
email.markdown:
Your code to open what {sender} shared with you is **{code}**.

Type it on the page within 10 minutes. It works once.

If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.

parts.about: One row of a list: the list's copy with only that row, its fields and rules as the list has them.
One saved view of a list: the list's copy with only the rows that view keeps right now, its fields and rules as the list has them, so the link shows what the view shows and never the rest.

addresses.about: A link's address (/share/<name>) is a name instead of a random code when the sharer chooses one, and for every link anyone may open (public) when they do not: the shared thing's first words, then those words with one more word (src/readable-names.json words, up to `more_word_tries` tries) when they are taken, claimed for the sharer in the one network-wide name list so no one else can take it. A name stays with the person who first claimed it; making a new link with it moves it to the new link and stops the old one. A link only its named recipient may open keeps its code unless the sharer names it: a secret name of random words (src/readable-names.mjs), so its address never tells a stranger it exists or what it opens. `listed` puts a public link's page in search results: it drops noindex, carries its own description and structured data, and can be found from /share/sitemap.xml, which links to smaller sitemap documents when many links are listed.
addresses.refused: An address is 3 to 64 lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, like spring-pricing.
addresses.taken: Someone else already uses that address. Choose another.
addresses.listed_needs_public: Only a link anyone may open can show in search results.
addresses.llms_about: Lists and records their owners chose to publish. Each entry links to its page; every page names who shared it.

adding.heading: Add files
adding.body: Choose the files to send. They go straight into {sender}'s folder; you will not see what else is in it.
adding.nothing: Choose at least one file to send.
adding.too_big: These files come to more than a page can send at once ({most}). Send fewer at a time; a bigger file goes from a computer or an AI through this same link.

signing.heading: Sign
signing.body: Type your full name to sign. Signing means you agree to these terms.
signing.refused_name: Type your full name to sign.

paying.received: Payment received. Your access is being set up. Refresh this page in a moment.

reading.about: A shared file of words opens as a page to read (src/record-share-pages.mjs): its words drawn by the one markdown renderer under its title, with Open file and Download after them. `markdown` names the media types and name endings read as markdown; `plain` the ones read as plain words whose line breaks are kept. At most `most_bytes` of the file are drawn, ending at the last whole line, and `more` says the rest is in the file.
reading.more: This page shows the first part. Open the file for the rest.
